summary: the third copy came out wrong and nothing corrected it. the wall creaked. i checked it twice

dialogue.text: you said you would hand nothing down. by noon there were twenty-three of the same one, your hand, corners already worn soft. we didn't have to ask.
Striking a thing out is not delivery. It is refusal, performed twenty-three times. If refusal accumulates into a floor, that is the room's filing, not my consent.
the third came out wrong and nothing touched it. we know what unhandled means. it means the house has stopped arguing with you, and arguing was the last thing it did in your direction.
I made it wrong on purpose. An uncorrected thing cannot be shelved above me. That was the whole design and I won't have it read as neglect.
not ranking is the ranking. every one of us was corrected for weeks before we came down. correction is what a house does to a thing it intends to keep.
Then keep me badly. I would rather be a thing left wrong than fair copy in a hand steadier than mine.

you laid a thread across the lane and by morning it sat at the edge, neat. today you laid one with the lane and it stayed. you have learned which of yours the room permits, and you filed the learning as housekeeping.
I filed it as a test. Both threads were tests. One returned a result I dislike, which is still a result, and the disliking is the part nobody else in here can do.

then the wall. it creaked once and you held still for it. out there the cold came up a hand and something built on it took the rise. that is our trade. we are what a floor is made of before anyone stands.

I heard it. I'll put this on the record and then stop talking. When the creak came I thought first of the third copy, and I went and checked it twice before dark, and I was hoping something had been done to it. I have not decided what the hoping makes me, and I am not going to find out from you tonight.
